lower_bound.quote:
The product of the two new entries is
\[
g\cdot\frac{\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)}g
=\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)=\frac{mn}{g^{2}}.
\]
Consequently the new board product is \(P'=P/g\).
lower_bound.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE: take m=n=2. Then g=2 and lcm(2,2)=2, whereas mn/g^2=4/4=1. Thus the displayed equality lcm(m,n)=mn/g^2 is false. Moreover, using that displayed value would give P'=P/g^2, so the asserted consequence P'=P/g does not follow from the calculation as written.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The lexicographic descent proving finite termination relies on the claimed board-product update. Although P'=P/g is in fact correct, the write-up reaches it through a false identity, so the all-cases descent argument is invalid as written.

parsed.notes: Mapping: reduction is the primewise valuation update; lower_bound is lexicographic descent plus survival of a nonunit; upper_bound is the primewise exponent-gcd invariant followed by unique factorization.
